subject.title: Add per-agent sandbox session visibility override feature

question: Should OpenClaw core accept `agents.list[].sandbox.sessionToolsVisibility` as a per-agent override for lifting the sandbox spawned-session clamp, or should this be folded into the broader per-agent session/A2A policy work first?
rationale: The code path is narrow and proof-backed, but it changes a core data-visibility boundary and overlaps other open per-agent access-control PRs, so automation should not decide the permanent policy shape.

options.title: Land the narrow clamp after rebase
options.body: Keep this PR as the focused implementation, require conflict resolution plus owner/security review, and preserve the default spawned-only behavior for all agents without the explicit override.

options.title: Fold into broader per-agent access work
options.body: Ask the author to rebase or transfer the sandbox clamp into the broader per-agent session/A2A design so all access policy lands through one config model.

options.title: Defer the config surface
options.body: Close or pause this PR until maintainers decide that per-agent sandbox visibility is part of the supported core security model.

recommendation.title: Land the narrow clamp after rebase
recommendation.body: Keep this PR as the focused implementation, require conflict resolution plus owner/security review, and preserve the default spawned-only behavior for all agents without the explicit override.

likelyOwner.reason: The current-main history for the touched session visibility helpers points to this owner, and the decision is core config/security policy.
